![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/11722616331__Web.jpg) 7. Connect lubricator pipes Connect and tighten the oil pipes for the cylinder lubrication. Activate the '*Lubricator test sequence*' on the MOP for the pertaining cylinder, see *description [6645-0260] 'Cylinder Lubricators'*. Vent the cylinder lubricating system by loosening the unions at the non-return valves until oil, without air bubbles, comes out from the pipes. ![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/assets/img/WarningEmbeddedBlack.png) CAUTION To minimise oil spray risk, use eye protection when venting the pipes. Tighten the unions. Check that there is no leakage from the system. Check that each individual lubricating point functions correctly by making a scavenge port inspection and that oil comes from each lubricator point, see *work card [3065-0601]*. Stop the '*Lubricator test sequence*' on the MOP. ![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/png/18014414739443339__Web.png) Copyright © 2024 MAN Energy Solutions * Home * Language * english * Home

﻿ Work during Repairs 1. 9836048 2. L9836048 3. Operation of Engine 4. Description 5. D50105-05 6. Work during Repairs ### Work during Repairs • **Crankshaft:** Carry out deflection measuring of the crankshaft, See "Checking of main bearings alignment (Autolog)", Working Card 510-01.00. • **Turbocharger:** If the recordings show that the charging air conditions have changed radically, cleaning of turbocharger or charge air cooler or other action should be effected, see separate instruction manual for turbocharger. • **Nuts and bolts:** Tighten all nuts and bolts in the crankcase, see "Data for torque moment", Description 500.40. Also retighten foundation bolts and check the chocks. • **Camshaft gear train:** Check the various gear wheels for the camshaft(s). • **Pneumatic valves:** Drain starting air pipes for condensed water. Check solenoid valve for overspeed stop and optionally, charge air by-pass valve and waste gate valve. • **Lub. oil cooler:** If the performance records indicate increased lub oil temperature or pressure drop, the oil cooler should be dismantled and cleaned.  8. Lubricating Condition ### Lubricating Condition Note if the “oil film” on the cylinder wall and piston rings appears to be adequate, see 'Cylinder Condition'. Black or brownish coloured areas may sometimes be seen on the liner surface. This indicates corrosive wear, usually from sulphuric acid (see the 'Corrosive wear' section), and should not be confused with grey-black areas, which indicates blow-by. These deposits are often only of cosmetic nature and will not lead to wear issues. The phenomenon is often connected to humidity in the scavenge air and may disappear when the vessel enters cold and less humid areas. For more information, see *description [2245-0090]* - 'Corrosive wear' and *description [3045-0110]*. Copyright © 2024 MAN Energy Solutions * Home * Language * english * Home

| Synopsis | Cyl 15. Prise above allowed value |
| Data Tree Path | ECU\*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Cyl 15. Prise above allowed value |
| Long Description | **Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.**{ALARM\_TEXT\_DEFINITION\_452\_Descrip} |
| Cause | **Too low Compression Pressure or too high Maximum Pressure**{ALARM\_TEXT\_DEFINITION\_449\_Cause} |
| Effect | **- Increased wear of cylinder liners - Risk of breakage of piston rings - Too high load on crosshead bearings**{ALARM\_TEXT\_DEFINITION\_450\_Effect} |
| Suggested Action | **Immediate Action: Reduce "Pmax Offset" on actual cylinder unit to lower Prise below alarm limit. Troubleshooting: 1.Check that current Pcomp "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances. If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset" on the actual cylinder unit manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation -&gtPcomp). 2.Check that current Pmax "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances. If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pmax Offset" for the actual cylinder unit manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation -&gtPmax). If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.**{ALARM\_TEXT\_DEFINITION\_451\_Action} |
